input: The recommendation under consideration is to install the scheduling system at Plant 2 first and hold the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported; the operations director owns the scheduling programme. The finding rests on order records for 12 months (13946 orders). On-time delivery over the last two quarters was 89%, against a target of 95%, and Plant 2 accounts for 56% of late orders, so the shortfall is concentrated rather than general. Overtime cost was $2.4 million last year, up 30% on the year before. The order backlog stands at 3.5 weeks, against 1.6 weeks a year ago, and the backlog has grown while delivery performance has stayed below target. The firm runs 4 plants, with revenue of $93 million per year. A scheduling system for all plants is quoted at $321k, against $112k for Plant 2 alone: the staged installation commits $112k to the plant where the late orders arise and holds the balance of the $321k until the Plant 2 result is known. An internal estimate, not a vendor figure, puts the overtime reduction at Plant 2 at 15–20% in the first year. The hold on the other plants is the control on the decision, and the overtime estimate is tested at one plant before it is relied on elsewhere.
